upper_bound_clamp.algorithm: when the upper_bound Slice* (this+0x80) is non-null and its length is non-zero, binary-search the key array (list+0x30, 16-byte Slice entries, one per seqnum index) over the fragment's [seq_idx_begin, seq_idx_end) range for the first entry with CompareTimestamp(entry, upper_bound) <= 0; the loop goes left when the comparison is <= 0 and right when it is > 0, so it assumes the key array is sorted with the comparison decreasing in the entry index; let consumed = that entry's index within the range; if the current seq offset (seq_ptr - (seq_base + begin*8)) / 8 >= consumed, keep the position; else set seq_ptr = seq_base + (begin + consumed)*8
upper_bound_clamp.builtin_noop: with the builtin comparators (slot 0xc8 = 0x5d48400, always 0) the search short-circuits before any comparison (the base pointer never moves, consumed = 0), so the clamp never fires; a timestamped comparator (slot 0xc8 returning a real ordering) makes the clamp cut the visible seq window at the first key-array entry whose timestamp comparison is <= 0, skipping the leading entries past the upper bound
